faq.question: Will converting JPG to PNG make the file larger?

faq.question: Does converting JPG to PNG add transparency?

faq.question: Can I convert multiple JPG files to PNG at once?

faq.answer: No, it uses a single effective tax rate you set rather than real tax brackets — use it for quick estimates, not exact payroll figures.

faq.question: What counts as a pre-tax deduction?
faq.answer: Things like 401(k) contributions or pre-tax health insurance premiums that reduce your taxable income.

faq.question: What pay frequencies are supported?
faq.answer: Weekly (52/year), biweekly (26/year), semi-monthly (24/year), and monthly (12/year).

faq.question: Why use an effective tax rate instead of exact tax brackets?
faq.answer: Real payroll tax calculations depend on filing status, state, and multiple bracket thresholds — this tool intentionally uses one simplified rate for a quick estimate rather than approximating complex, jurisdiction-specific tax logic.

faq.question: What's the difference between gross and net pay here?
faq.answer: Gross pay is your salary divided by pay periods before any deductions; net pay is what's left after pre-tax deductions and estimated taxes are subtracted.

faq.question: How do I estimate my effective tax rate?
faq.answer: Divide your total expected annual tax (federal, state, and FICA combined) by your gross annual income — your last pay stub or tax return is a good reference point.

faq.question: Does semi-monthly mean the same as biweekly?
faq.answer: No — semi-monthly is 24 pay periods a year (twice a month, e.g. the 1st and 15th), while biweekly is 26 pay periods (every two weeks), which changes the amount per paycheck even for the same annual salary.
